items.summary: With Democrats poised to control both chambers of Congress, the party faces a defining challenge: how to constrain Donald Trump's presidency while carving out a path to the White House in 2028. For Ian Reifowitz, Distinguished Professor of History at SUNY Empire State University, the answer lies in drawing on the historical legacy of Franklin D. Roosevelt's New Deal coalition. Republicans, he argues, have progressively shifted electoral competition towards questions of identity, immigration and cultural conflict. Democrats, by contrast, must recover their traditional strength on economic security, affordability and everyday living standards. "These Democrats across the country ran on affordability." And that's how they must govern, explains Reifowitz.

The results have been accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics. The paper is currently available on the arXiv preprint server.

MPs told it's crunch time for a decision on refurbishment amid warnings of a Notre Dame-style fire. More asbestos has been discovered in Parliament, the BBC has learnt, as MPs come under pressure to sign off on a major revamp of the crumbling home of UK democracy. Known asbestos items in the Palace of Westminster and wider parliamentary estate, such as insulation, roofing, floor tiles and ropes, now number more than 1,650 - an increase of 500 since 2021. It comes as the government considers holding a vote on refurbishing Parliament, which could cost up to £40bn and take 61 years, after years of indecision and delay.

Five of France's unions have joined a wave of strikes and protests in a national day of action. Hundreds of thousands of demonstrators are expected to take part in marches across France as five unions join strikes and protests in a national day of action. The protests began in September with high school students complaining about poor conditions and resources in education, but have spread to include the so-called "yellow vest" movement and workers. Authorities expect 500,000 to 700,000 demonstrators to join marches, with tens of thousands more in Paris alone, in a day billed by one union leader as "a great day of convergence".

Huge, ecstatic canvases are just one of the vocations of the musician who joined the art rockers in 2024. As her show Hotwire My Heart opens, she talks terror, awe and teabags E mma Richardson loves to eavesdrop when people look at her paintings and talk about what they see in them. “They turn into these Rorschach inkblot tests,” she grins. Looking at her works, you do stand back in awe wondering. Is that a nebula, a god or a fleshy, baroque orgy? An explosion, an implosion or an orgasm? Richardson implies all of these and more, her paintbrush chasing in vivid oils the hedonism, desire and breadth of human experience.

Wong, 30, is among hundreds of Hongkongers detained under the controversial national security law. Joshua Wong, once the face of Hong Kong's democracy movement, has been sentenced to 10 years in jail for colluding with foreign forces under the city's sweeping national security law. Wong is among hundreds of campaigners and ordinary Hongkongers arrested under the law, which was imposed in 2020 following explosive pro-democracy protests against Beijing's growing control. Critics say the far-reaching law has silenced dissent, but authorities argue that it is needed to maintain stability and deny it has weakened the city's cherished autonomy.

Concacaf's new Gold Cup format will feature two groups of eight teams, with the change designed to create more meaningful matchups during the group stage. Previously played with four groups of four, the 2027 edition of the competition will have two groups of eight with teams sorted into "ranking bands." Teams will play four group matches instead of the previous three, with the top four teams in each group moving into the quarterfinals. The bands will separate teams into levels based on their Concacaf ranking. Teams will meet an opponent from each band, meaning the strongest team in a group will play a team from Band 2, Band 3 and Band 4.

The ocean’s blue and green hues near the infamous zone of debris have gotten brighter over the last 20 years, satellite data show The Great Pacific Garbage Patch , an area in the Pacific Ocean where debris naturally accumulates, is full of tiny bits of plastic. So full, in fact, that it seems to be changing the color of the ocean. The ocean is, of course, famously blue. That’s due to the wavelength of light it reflects . Water scatters shorter wavelengths, which we see as blue—while absorbing longer wavelengths such as red or orange. Additives in the ocean can affect its color, including phytoplankton, algae and sediment.

Using a capture card and open-source software to run PS5 video through a PC GPU. On an explicitly unmoderated GTAVI subreddit, user RevolutionaryBus8208 lays out a proposed setup, which runs a PS5 through a 4K capture card to a PC. From there, the video signal is run through Veyra , an open source tool that can apply DLSS 5’s AI-powered “neural rendering” to video content. The result—which also uses DLSS frame generation to increase the 30 fps source to a 90 fps output—is then piped back to a 4K TV, theoretically adding some of the benefits of a beefy PC graphics card to a console-exclusive game.

Software optimizes a physical model of the telescope to reduce noise. While telescopes can be fitted with devices called coronagraphs that block out much of a star’s light, there are limits to their effectiveness, caused by noise from subtle variations in the telescope’s configuration and pointing between observations. Now, researchers have developed a new software package that optimizes a physical model of the telescope in a way that allows us to better model these differences, producing low-noise imaging of exoplanets.

LIV Golf appears to be over, with it announced this week that it will enter liquidation. But how has it got to this point for the breakaway league that threw huge sums of money at the sport and played the role of major disruptor when it entered onto the scene five years ago. Tributes have been paid to Michael Locke, star of MTV stunt and prank series Dirty Sanchez, who has died aged 47. Locke, from Port Talbot, known as 'Pancho', starred in the show, and later went on to launch the Welsh clothing brand San Portablo .
